Description: Health 1. When you destroy it, every enemy within 2 squares takes 2 damage. It is whole again at the start of your next game
What it is there: Ten runestones stand on the Runenberg map; each night they regenerate their magic, only heroes can break them (or an enemy's area attack, by accident), and a broken one damages every enemy within two tiles.
Why it fits: A placed bomb you choose when to set off, which comes back every game; units are the thinnest sheet.
Needs: new: a unit that comes back

Name: Devil's Lodge
Description: A room of red velvet and smoke on a pirate ship. Something behind the curtain is willing to deal.
Choices: Take a random curse: Gain +1 Small Chest | Leave
What it is there: A pirate spaceship room where you can choose to be randomly cursed for a chest with a random perk; curses are how you reach a Ghost Ship, so players take them on purpose.
Why it fits: A curse traded for a chest, which turns curses into something you might want (with the Evil-Devouring Sword).

Name: One-eyed Sam
Description: Everything you could want, behind a counter you'll never rob.
Choices: Shelf of six pieces, two of each Rarity, at five times the price | Leave
What it is there: The black market, through a portal between levels 22 and 23: a shop covering most of a level that sells a wide variety at 25 times the usual price (50 for magic items), kept by One-eyed Sam, who wields Thiefbane and wears most of an ascension kit, with nine named monster assistants.
Why it fits: A shop where nothing is out of stock and everything costs too much: gold saved all run finally has somewhere to go.

Name: Machineland
Description: When entered, spawn 1 random robot tagged Enemy and 1 random rodent tagged Enemy. Robot things turn up 30% more often.
What it is there: The first biome: an arms corporation that 'specializes in the commercial supply of mechanized rodents and marsupials': Hamster Bombs, Roborabbits, Automated Rats, Ferret Turrets, Beaver Saws.
Why it fits: An arms corporation that supplies mechanised rodents. One of each.

Name: Banner of Fury
Description: Stands where the first enemy of a game fell. While it stands, your Weapons gain +1 Stun
What it is there: A Tiger Banner Aura Aspect: 'Spawn a Banner in the spot of first killed enemy in each room that grants 5% additional Base Damage to everyone in radius.' Jaguar's Call of the Wind does the same with dodge.
Why it fits: A placed unit that helps you rather than hurting enemies; units are the thinnest sheet (1 row).
Needs: new: a unit laid where an enemy was defeated

Name: Infested Nest
Description: When entered, spawn 1 random bug tagged Enemy and 2 Web tiles on random tiles. Bug things turn up 30% more often.
What it is there: A battle type fought in narrow combat areas against the insect enemies (Lethal Venomflies, Vicious Venom Bugs, Crimson Spiders), with a boss and more enemies when the ship arrives.
Why it fits: Narrow combat areas against insects. Clones The Hive's bugs but adds the nest's webbing, so the two can sit at different tiers.
Builds on: spawn_enemy, Web tile, bug tag (5 bodies)

Name: Execution Gallows
Description: The State's gallows, with a prisoner on the platform and the colony watching.
Choices: Hang the prisoner: every enemy of your next game is Stunned on its first turn, but Lose 1 Max Health | Pardon them: Gain +1 Health | Leave
What it is there: A base building. Prisoners can be 'crushed through fear, indoctrination, execution, or conversion', and an execution is 'a warning to would-be rebels'. 'Decide who eats, and who gets hanged.'
Why it fits: Objects are things you stand at and choose (2 rows). Fear against mercy is the game's own satire.

Name: Ekeko
Description: Sells a bit of everything: weapons, jewellery, potions.
Choices: Shelf of mixed stock | Fight him: start a game against him for his soul and the shelf
What it is there: A creation of the Warlock met in the Abyss. He sells weapons, spare monster souls, rings, bracelets and necklaces, health and mana potions and Camp Tokens, and 'can also be fought for a chance to capture his soul'. Named after the Andean god of fortune and prosperity.
Why it fits: Named shopkeepers are planned (spec §14.5); a shopkeeper you can turn on is Ekeko's twist, and a god of prosperity is a good face for a shop.

Name: Hidden Shrine
Description: A shrine half-buried in the dungeon wall.
Choices: Pray: a random Weapon in your pack loses 2 Stun for the run; every other Weapon Gains +1 Stun | Leave
What it is there: One of Diablo I's shrines, 'New strength is forged through destruction': -10 current and max durability to a random equipped item, +10 to all others.
Why it fits: A shrine that sacrifices one piece to strengthen the rest, so it is worth more the more Weapons you carry. Enchanted Shrine is its spell twin (every spell up a level, one random spell down).
Builds on: Goat Shrine and Fountain of Tears (Diablo's shrines on the sheet), weapon_stun

Name: Valda's Statue
Description: A statue of Valda, the entombed god of souls, Adis' twin.
Choices: Pray: Gain a Curse and +1 Large Chest | Leave
What it is there: Valda is one of the entombed gods, found in the Tomb of Souls in Lisveden; players can visit her statue there.
Why it fits: A god of souls who asks for something back: a shrine that pays well and costs a curse, joining the shrine objects.
